name: אֶבְיָתָר
gloss: the father is pre-eminent; or father of abundance
summary: Abiathar son of Ahimelech, of the house of Eli, the one son who escaped when Saul had the priests of Nob killed, and fled to David with the ephod (1Sa 22:20; 23:6). He was priest with Zadok through David's reign and carried the ark with him when David fled from Absalom (2Sa 15:24, 29), but sided with Adonijah, and Solomon thrust him out of the priesthood “to fulfil the word of Yahweh that he spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh” (1Ki 2:26–27; 1Sa 2:31–36). Jesus names him in Mrk 2:26 (Ἀβιαθάρ; the Peshitta writes אַבִֿיתָֿר). The name is אָב “father” with יָתָר, a form of יתר “be over, excel”: “the father is pre-eminent” or “father of abundance”; scripture does not explain it, though his story is of the one left (1Sa 22:20) of Eli's house, every one of whom was to be “הַנּוֹתָר” in it (1Sa 2:36).

evidence.note: “One son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was אֶבְיָתָר; and he fled after David.”
“When אֶבְיָתָר son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he came down with an ephod in his hand.”
With Zadok and the ark when David left Jerusalem.
Solomon thrust out אֶבְיָתָר from being priest to Yahweh, fulfilling the word spoken of the house of Eli.
“Everyone הַנּוֹתָר in your house will come to bow down to him for a piece of silver”: the word against Eli's house.
“In the days of Abiathar the high priest”, David ate the showbread.
The noun יֶתֶר, “pre-eminence”, of the same root.

note: Takes a.ae.bc, which BDB files under אבה with the gloss “the Great One is father (?)”; it is placed under יתר here because the second element is יָתָר, and no other entry claims the key. The reading of יָתָר (a verbal adjective “is pre-eminent”, or a noun “abundance”) is a reading of the form only. Mrk 2:26 names Abiathar where 1Sa 21:1 has Ahimelech; that is left to the reviewer.
